newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH MONEY MARKET CALM WITH SUMMER APPROACHING.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH MONEY MARKET CALM WITH SUMMER APPROACHING.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were virtually unchanged on Wednesday, in a relatively calm market.
Dealers said the approach of the summer was starting to have an impact on the volume of business.
Call money broadly held on to Tuesday's levels, bid around 3.00 percent and said to change hands around 3.06 percent.
Three-month deposits stood at 3.12/20 percent bid/ask.
Dealers said there was little to no activity at all in Dutch Treasury certificates (DTCs) - no surprise as the Finance Ministry's Agent seemed not in need of funds at the moment.
"They're on the offer side in short money, since tax payments have just come in," one dealer said, adding DTCs therefore remained priced quite defensively.

DTCs maturing end August were set at an indicative price of 3.07 percent, those of September at 3.09 percent, those of December at 3.12 percent, while DTCs running until June 30, 1998 were set at 3.21 percent.
The guilder traded at 112.564 per 100 marks, slightly weaker than on Tuesday.
